## Main finding

The two-step nilpotent clause of Heib–Bruschi's minimal-graph-admissibility
conjecture has complete ordinary counterarguments in this lane:

- `PROOF.md`: a generic 12-dimensional real or complex counterexample. The
  112 independent bracket coefficients cannot come from any of the polynomial
  charts for multiplicative bases, each with only 108 parameters.
- `PRIOR_METHOD.md`: an explicit rational 20-dimensional counterexample,
  obtained by the exterior-square version of a public 2016 rank obstruction.
  This second route exposes the strongest objection to discovery eligibility.

Exact target: [arXiv:2601.16161v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.16161v2),
Definition 15, equation (6), printed/PDF p.7, Conjecture 91(a), p.62;
[MathDB 372720](https://mathdb.com/api/posts/372720). The definition requires an
actual basis, not a redundant spanning set. The two key PDF pages were rendered
and visually inspected; images are under `verification/`.

**Recommendation: do not count this as a genuine new discovery.** A
[2016 public answer](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1858832/does-every-finite-dimensional-real-nil-algebra-admit-a-multiplicative-basis)
already gives the closely corresponding symmetric-algebra rank obstruction.
The exterior-square transfer is short and complete. The public answer does
not literally state the Lie result, and no such literal prior statement was
located in the bounded search. Nevertheless, this presents a serious
routine-adaptation objection under the user's standard. The smaller generic
dimension is not nominated as a separate result.

    sum_{n>=1} psi_n(X) t^n/n!

# astra-discrete-r3 handoff

**One candidate mathematical resolution; zero accepted credit.**

Candidate: full An–Đoković Conjecture3.6 (MathDB381028), for every n≥2 and 1≤k<n:

⟨χ_(J_(k,n)), Δ_n⟩ = (−1)^(n−1) C(n,k) C(n−2,k−1).

The exact source, quantifiers, complete written proof, and a self-contained proof of the needed restricted divided-symmetrization lemma are in **discovery.md**. This is an all-n claim, not the already public n≤12 verification or Narayana observation.

## Core idea

Cancel the adjacent Vandermonde factors to obtain the degree n−1 numerator
P=∏_(j≤k)(x_n−x_j) ∏_(k<i<n)(x_i−x_1).
Its internal exponents are at most one, so the negative-prefix set of each monomial is a terminal interval. The classical monomial DS value is therefore the signed binomial weight w_r=(−1)^(n−r)C(n−1,r−1). For the cumulative coefficient mass C_j, specialize x_1,…,x_j=t and all later variables to1. The whole product vanishes unless j=k, when it is (1−t)^(n−1). Thus only first-deficit classes k and k+1 survive; an alternating-binomial-tail identity and Pascal give the exact result.

```lean
(p : Matrix N I ℂ) (r : Matrix N R ℂ)
(q : Matrix N J ℂ) (s : Matrix N S ℂ)
(hp : pᴴ * p = 1) (hr : rᴴ * r = 1)

(hpq : pᴴ * q = 0) (hrs : rᴴ * s = 0)
```

It proves the literal conclusion:

```lean
let P := p * pᴴ
let R := r * rᴴ
let Q := q * qᴴ
let S := s * sᴴ
let P' := mpInvSqrt (P + R) * P * mpInvSqrt (P + R)
let R' := mpInvSqrt (P + R) * R * mpInvSqrt (P + R)
let Q' := mpInvSqrt (Q + S) * Q * mpInvSqrt (Q + S)
let S' := mpInvSqrt (Q + S) * S * mpInvSqrt (Q + S)
(Matrix.trace (P' * Q' + R' * S')).re ≤
  (Matrix.trace (P * R + Q * S)).re
```

## Core idea

Cancel the adjacent Vandermonde factors to obtain the degree n−1 numerator
P=∏_(j≤k)(x_n−x_j) ∏_(k<i<n)(x_i−x_1).
Its internal exponents are at most one, so the negative-prefix set of each monomial is a terminal interval. The whole product vanishes unless j=k, when it is (1−t)^(n−1). Thus only first-deficit classes k and k+1 survive; an alternating-binomial-tail identity and Pascal give the exact result.
